Build dev project

Source: R/build.R
projr_build_dev.Rd

Runs the selected scripts and renders documents for development. Development builds preserve the project's version and can run before its first versioned build. Staged outputs are available in the build cache.

Usage

projr_build_dev(
  scripts = NULL,
  bump = FALSE,
  old_dev_remove = TRUE,
  args_engine = list(),
  profile = NULL,
  pipeline = NULL,
  clear_output = "never",
  project = NULL
)

Arguments

scripts

character vector. Paths or glob patterns for scripts to build, relative to the project root or absolute. Prefix a pattern with ! to exclude matches. Use an empty character vector or "" to skip running scripts. With a pipeline selected, these scripts take the place of dev.scripts and combine with the pipeline's; add pipeline = FALSE to run only them. The default, NULL, checks dev.scripts and then build.scripts. If neither is set, a Quarto or Bookdown project renders before automatically detected R scripts. Without a project, scripts are detected in the project root and run alphabetically. When every entry is an exclusion, use these automatic rules and skip the matching files. In a YAML scripts list, use an entry such as - exclude: scratch.R or a quoted string such as "!scratch.R".

Explicit selections run in order, with each glob expanded alphabetically. Listing an R script or standalone document twice runs it twice. A repeated project document is an error. If a selection includes Quarto or Bookdown project documents, those documents render together at the position of the last selected project document. The project YAML is restored after rendering and post-build hooks.

bump

logical. Retained for compatibility. Supplying TRUE warns and runs a development build with the project's existing version, if any.

old_dev_remove

logical. If TRUE, then previous development builds are deleted after a successful run.

args_engine

List of options for the selected build engines. For one engine, use its native arguments directly, e.g. list(quiet = TRUE) for one or more standalone R Markdown documents. When multiple engines run, group options by engine, e.g. list(quarto_project = list(profile = "print"), rmd = list(quiet = TRUE)). Use quarto_project or quarto_document for quarto::quarto_render(), rmd for rmarkdown::render() and bookdown for bookdown::render_book(). Plain R scripts (r) take no render options. Omit any engine to use its defaults. The default list() works for any selection. Quarto renders in the foreground so later scripts and hooks see its output.

profile

character. projr profile to use. Sets PROJR_PROFILE for the build, so it overrides that variable and the profile key in _projr-local.yml and _projr.yml.

pipeline

character. Names of pipelines under pipelines to run in order, or FALSE to run none. Entries can be globs; a glob's matches run in their order under pipelines, and each pipeline runs once. Overrides build.pipeline (or dev.pipeline for development builds) for this build. Inline scripts and hooks, and the scripts argument of projr_build_dev(), still combine with it. Default is NULL, using the configured selection.

clear_output

character. When to clear output directories: "pre" (before build), "post" (after build), or "never" (default for dev builds). Can also be set via PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT environment variable.

project

Path to the project root. The default discovers the project from the working directory. The first interactive build asks permission to run its scripts and hooks, change project files and publish configured outputs. projr remembers approval for this checkout in the user's R configuration directory. In a noninteractive session, pass the root explicitly (for example, project = ".") to authorize this build without saving approval.

Value

Invisibly returns TRUE after a successful build.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
projr_build_dev(scripts = c("reports/*.Rmd", "!reports/draft.Rmd"))
} # }
